quotes.text: Efficiency doesn't come from hitting enabled. It comes from asking the harder question right at the beginning. Do we need a copilot studio agent that reflects our processes or language and our data.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames the central decision question before building any custom agent.

quotes.text: Defining personas isn't a fluffy exercise. It's the foundation that makes the rest of the project possible.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise argument for starting agent design with personas.

quotes.text: Just because you can automate minor questions doesn't mean it's worth the effort of building, training and maintaining that automation.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: This is why the line between a chatbot and a copilot matters. A chatbot holds conversations. A copilot takes context, combines it with actions, and turns it into support that people trust.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear distinction between a conversational bot and a grounded, action-taking agent.

quotes.text: The hardest decision in a co pilot project isn't how to build it. It's deciding if you actually need one.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable summary of the episode's core message.

takeaways: Generic, quickly deployed copilots often stall because they lack role-specific context and grounding in company data.
Clear personas and a short list of use cases scored by value, frequency and feasibility decide whether a dedicated Copilot Studio agent is worth building.
Knowledge grounding plus action-taking skills, a phased pilot rollout and internal champions turn an agent into a trusted everyday tool.
hook: Many organizations rush into AI agents and end up with tools nobody uses. This episode helps business and IT leaders decide whether they really need a Copilot Studio agent by starting from personas and real use cases, and shows how grounding, skills and a structured rollout drive adoption.
